sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression of myc-tagged EpoR variants confirmed by anti-myc flow cytometry (L1, chimeric constructs); surface expression of the full-length hEpoR myc-tagged construct is NOT MEASURED in the ledger clips.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly states that the full-length hEpoR expression vector retains both the N-terminal signal peptide and a myc tag, placing the tag at the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage. EPOR has a single-pass topology with one extracellular terminus (residues 25–250), so the tag position is unambiguous: it follows the SP cleavage site at residue 24 (W) and precedes the mature protein starting at residue 25 (A). Python verification confirms res(24)=W and res(25)=A. The tag is 226 residues from the TM boundary (residue 251), well clear of any steric constraint. Full-length hEpoR expression vector retaining the N-terminal signal peptide and a myc tag, described in PMC13505329. The same paper (L1) confirms surface expression of myc-tagged EpoR variants by flow cytometry in Ba/F3-gp130 cells, though those flow-cytometry constructs are chimeric (VHH replacing D1). The full-length hEpoR construct with myc tag is described at the vector level (L2); no residue number is stated, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists (mature N-terminus, residue 25), so the junction is computed from the signal-peptide landmark: insert_after_residue = 24 (last residue of SP = W; first residue of mature protein = A25).

sources.claim: For hEpoR, the N-terminal signal peptide and myc tag remained in the vector after linearization.

literature_notes: L1 describes myc-tagged chimeric EpoR variants (G VHH EpoRΔD1 series) in which domain 1 of EpoR is replaced by a VHH nanobody; these are not standard full-length EPOR and the myc tag position cannot be mapped to a specific residue in the canonical EPOR sequence. L1 therefore cannot independently pin a second site. The intracellular tyrosine residues mentioned in L1 (Y426, Y454, Y456, and the ΔY426–S480 / ΔY454–S480 truncations) are deletion/mutation targets in the intracellular domain (residues 273–508) and are not tag-insertion sites; they are excluded from both sites and other_positions. Only one surface tag site is supported by the ledger.
